taxonomy.note: Accepted as a distinct central-Texas endemic in FNA/ITIS/NatureServe and current regional treatments.

evidence: Travis — NatureServe and the UT PRC Travis County herbarium document Matelea edwardsensis.
Bell — NatureServe explicitly lists Bell County records.
Comal — NatureServe explicitly lists Comal County records.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide or ecoregion range. Legacy names are counted only where taxonomic concept is reconciled.

morphology.look_here_first: Compare the flower directly with pearl milkvine: it is more bell-shaped, with mostly parallel longitudinal green lines that become netted only near the lobe tips/margins, and the inner corolla surface is visibly hairy.
diagnostic_traits: stems sparsely hairy to nearly glabrous
deeply cordate opposite leaves, basal lobes often overlapping
pale yellow-green campanulate corolla with darker longitudinal lines
five fleshy corona segments free nearly to base

confusers.separator: M. edwardsensis is less hairy and has a campanulate, longitudinally lined, hairy-inside flower with distinct corona segments; M. reticulata is flat, broadly netted, glabrous inside, and has a reduced corona plus a silvery center.
C. biflora is a low hairy herb with paired dark flowers; M. edwardsensis is a twining vine with pale green lined flowers.
